_about: Mechanism classes of the screened compounds. Code reads them (tahoemap/mechanisms.py); nobody edits a result by hand. A drug is in a class by one of three routes, and every membership names its route: a code constant below ('molecule_classes', by the molecule's name, so it also works offline), a ChEMBL mechanism rule ('mechanism_rules': the action type, mechanism text and target ChEMBL curates), or a WHO ATC code that ChEMBL reports for the molecule ('atc_rules'). Tahoe's own annotation is never changed and never makes a class: it is shown next to these classes, with an alert where the two disagree. Every class, rule and constant cites its source (with its DOI where it is a paper). 'effect' says what the class does to the cell's read-out: 'trap' (the drug traps its target on DNA or freezes it, so its effects are not those of losing the target), 'dna' (the drug damages or binds DNA itself), 'translation' (the drug stops protein synthesis, which raises many short-lived mRNAs whatever their pathway), 'none' (an ordinary inhibitor or agonist). 'targets' lists the genes the class acts on (HGNC symbols, or one regular expression starting with '^'); 'verb' says, for a trap class, what the drug does to such a target. 'plural' is the label as a plural noun phrase, for sentences that name the drugs of a class (a module label: 'raised by glucocorticoid receptor agonists').

TOP1_POISON.label: TOP1 poison (traps TOP1 on DNA)
TOP1_POISON.plural: TOP1 poisons (they trap TOP1 on DNA)
TOP1_POISON.why: the drug traps TOP1 on DNA and breaks DNA; its effects are those of the damage, not of TOP1 loss

TOP2_POISON.label: TOP2 poison (traps TOP2 on DNA)
TOP2_POISON.plural: TOP2 poisons (they trap TOP2 on DNA)
TOP2_POISON.why: the drug traps TOP2 on DNA and breaks DNA; its effects are those of the damage, not of TOP2 loss
TOP2_POISON.source: Nitiss JL 2009, Nat Rev Cancer 9:338 (doi:10.1038/nrc2607); Pommier Y, Leo E, Zhang H, Marchand C 2010, Chem Biol 17:421 (doi:10.1016/j.chembiol.2010.04.012)

PARP_TRAPPER.label: PARP inhibitor (also traps PARP on DNA)
PARP_TRAPPER.plural: PARP inhibitors (they also trap PARP on DNA)
PARP_TRAPPER.why: the drug traps PARP1/2 on DNA; trapped PARP is more toxic than PARP loss

TUBULIN_STABILISER.label: microtubule stabiliser (taxane)
TUBULIN_STABILISER.why: the drug binds tubulin in microtubules and stops them coming apart, so mitosis arrests; its effects are not those of losing a tubulin gene
TUBULIN_STABILISER.source: Jordan MA, Wilson L 2004, Nat Rev Cancer 4:253 (doi:10.1038/nrc1317)

TUBULIN_DESTABILISER.label: microtubule destabiliser
TUBULIN_DESTABILISER.why: the drug binds tubulin and stops it forming microtubules (or takes them apart), so mitosis arrests: like less working tubulin
TUBULIN_DESTABILISER.source: Jordan MA, Wilson L 2004, Nat Rev Cancer 4:253 (doi:10.1038/nrc1317)

DNA_ALKYLATOR.label: alkylates or cross-links DNA
DNA_ALKYLATOR.plural: drugs that alkylate or cross-link DNA
DNA_ALKYLATOR.source: WHO ATC L01A, L01XA; ChEMBL action type

DNA_INTERCALATOR.label: intercalates into DNA
DNA_INTERCALATOR.source: WHO ATC L01DB; ChEMBL action type INTERCALATING AGENT

DNA_BINDER.label: acts on DNA directly (ChEMBL target: DNA)
DNA_BINDER.plural: drugs that act on DNA directly (ChEMBL target: DNA)
DNA_BINDER.why: ChEMBL names DNA itself as the target

ANTIMETABOLITE.label: antimetabolite (blocks nucleotide or DNA synthesis)
ANTIMETABOLITE.plural: antimetabolites (they block nucleotide or DNA synthesis)
ANTIMETABOLITE.why: the drug starves or stalls DNA synthesis
ANTIMETABOLITE.source: WHO ATC L01B; ChEMBL mechanism targets

TRANSLATION_ELONGATION.label: translation inhibitor (blocks the ribosome)
TRANSLATION_ELONGATION.why: the drug stops protein synthesis; this stabilises and raises (superinduces) short-lived mRNAs, so a rise may not be activation of the gene's pathway
TRANSLATION_ELONGATION.source: Edwards DR, Mahadevan LC 1992, EMBO J 11:2415 (doi:10.1002/j.1460-2075.1992.tb05306.x): protein synthesis inhibitors superinduce short-lived mRNAs

GR_AGONIST.label: glucocorticoid receptor agonist
GR_AGONIST.source: ChEMBL mechanism on NR3C1; WHO ATC H02AB, D07A

PROTEASOME_INHIBITOR.label: proteasome inhibitor
PROTEASOME_INHIBITOR.source: ChEMBL mechanism on the proteasome; WHO ATC L01XG

HDAC_INHIBITOR.label: histone deacetylase inhibitor
HDAC_INHIBITOR.source: ChEMBL mechanism on histone deacetylases; WHO ATC L01XH

HMGCR_INHIBITOR.label: HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor (statin)
HMGCR_INHIBITOR.source: ChEMBL mechanism on HMGCR; WHO ATC C10AA

SMO_INHIBITOR.label: Smoothened (Hedgehog pathway) inhibitor
SMO_INHIBITOR.source: ChEMBL mechanism on SMO; WHO ATC L01XJ

action_direction._about: ChEMBL action types read as raising (up) or lowering (down) the target's activity; any other type: no direction
action_direction.source: ChEMBL action types (ChEMBL web services, action_type)

mechanism_rules.source: ChEMBL mechanism on TOP1; every clinical TOP1 inhibitor (camptothecins) traps TOP1 on DNA (Pommier 2006)
ChEMBL mechanism on TOP2A/TOP2B; anthracyclines, anthracenediones, amsacrine and epipodophyllotoxins trap TOP2 on DNA; the catalytic inhibitors listed in except_molecules do not (Nitiss 2009)
ChEMBL mechanism on PARP1/2; clinical PARP inhibitors trap PARP on DNA (Murai 2012)
ChEMBL mechanism on tubulin with action type STABILISER (Jordan and Wilson 2004)
ChEMBL mechanism on tubulin whose text says it stabilises (Jordan and Wilson 2004)
ChEMBL mechanism on tubulin (any species); a drug that is also a stabiliser keeps only TUBULIN_STABILISER (Jordan and Wilson 2004)

mechanism_rules.target_name_regex: dihydrofolate reductase|thymidylate synthase|ribonucleoside-diphosphate reductase|DNA polymerase|GAR transformylase|purine biosynthetic
mechanism_rules.source: ChEMBL mechanism on a nucleotide or DNA synthesis enzyme
ChEMBL mechanism: a eukaryotic ribosome, inhibited

molecule_classes._about: Core members of some classes, by molecule key (mechanisms.molecule_key: the name without its salt, upper case), each with its source. They make a class work offline, before ChEMBL is loaded, and for screened compounds ChEMBL gives no mechanism for. A key matches the Tahoe name and the matched ChEMBL name.

not_members._about: Compounds that are NOT in a class although a label might suggest it, with the reason. This list documents a decision; it removes no data and no membership. Tahoe's moa-fine label 'Protein synthesis inhibitor' is not a class rule: it also covers these four MNK / eIF4E inhibitors, which slow the translation of some mRNAs but do not stop protein synthesis, and in the real data they show no superinduction: in tables/drug_effects of the real run, 4EGI-1 has one immediate-early gene row, Tomivosertib, ETC-206 and SBI-0640756 none, while Harringtonine raises 36 and Homoharringtonine 42 such rows.
not_members._source: Tahoe-100M drug metadata (moa-fine); ChEMBL mechanisms; tables/drug_effects of the real run (immediate-early genes: tahoemap/data/control_sets.json IMMEDIATE_EARLY)

TRANSLATION_ELONGATION.TOMIVOSERTIB: MNK1/2 inhibitor (ChEMBL): slows cap-dependent translation of some mRNAs; does not stop protein synthesis
TRANSLATION_ELONGATION.ETC-206: MNK1/2 inhibitor (ChEMBL): slows cap-dependent translation of some mRNAs; does not stop protein synthesis
TRANSLATION_ELONGATION.4EGI-1: blocks eIF4E-eIF4G binding: slows cap-dependent translation of some mRNAs; does not stop protein synthesis
TRANSLATION_ELONGATION.SBI-0640756: blocks eIF4E-eIF4G binding: slows cap-dependent translation of some mRNAs; does not stop protein synthesis

tahoe_moa_classes._about: Tahoe moa_fine labels that name a class, and the classes that agree with each. Used only to compare the two sources (an alert where they disagree), never to make a class. A label not listed agrees or disagrees on targets only.
tahoe_moa_classes._source: Tahoe-100M drug metadata (moa-fine), read against the classes above

linked_targets.why: KEAP1 holds NRF2 (NFE2L2) for degradation; blocking KEAP1 activates NRF2
linked_targets.source: Itoh K et al. 1999, Genes Dev 13:76 (doi:10.1101/gad.13.1.76)

linked_targets.why: rapalogs bind FKBP12 (FKBP1A), and the pair inhibits mTOR
cyclosporin binds cyclophilin A (PPIA), and the pair inhibits calcineurin
farnesyltransferase (FNTA/FNTB) attaches the lipid RAS needs at the membrane
